nodes.label: Render Blueprint (render.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure-as-code Blueprint so the backend + managed Postgres can be imported into Render in one step instead of hand-wiring the dashboard.

nodes.label: bookit-db (Render managed Postgres, free plan, oregon)
nodes.rationale: Managed Postgres on the free tier, pinned to the same region as the backend to keep DB latency low.

nodes.label: bookit-backend (Render docker web service, free plan, oregon)
nodes.rationale: Docker runtime rather than a native Java runtime, so the JVM/Maven build is reproducible from the repo Dockerfile.

nodes.label: dockerfilePath / dockerContext -> ./app/backend
nodes.rationale: Monorepo: the docker context is scoped to the backend subfolder so the frontend is not shipped into the backend image.

nodes.label: healthCheckPath: /api/services
nodes.rationale: A public, DB-backed GET endpoint is used as the liveness probe, so a green health check also proves the datasource is reachable.

nodes.label: DB_HOST / DB_PORT / DB_NAME / DB_USER / DB_PASSWORD (fromDatabase: bookit-db)
nodes.rationale: Connection values are injected by Render from the linked database rather than typed in, so no DB credential ever lives in the repo. Values are managed by Render and not present in source (redacted).

nodes.label: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI (pinned https://bookit-backend.onrender.com/api/google/oauth2/callback)
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: the URL is deterministic because the service name is pinned, so the OAuth redirect can be committed rather than filled in after the first deploy.

nodes.label: sync:false secrets (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, JWT_SECRET, EMAIL_USER, EMAIL_PASS)
nodes.rationale: sync:false declares the key without a value so the Blueprint import prompts for it; secret VALUES are deliberately absent from the repo (redacted).

nodes.label: APP_CORS_ORIGINS (sync:false, set to the Vercel URL post-deploy)
nodes.rationale: Declared as a placeholder so the import prompts for it; the real frontend origin is only known after the Vercel deploy. Value redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: Backend application.yaml
nodes.rationale: Single config surface; every secret is env-var-bound with a dev-safe default so the same file works locally and on Render.

nodes.label: server.port: ${PORT:8080}
nodes.rationale: Comment: Render and most PaaS hosts inject PORT and require the app to bind to it; 8080 is the local fallback where PORT is unset.

nodes.label: spring.datasource url/username/password (DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD)
nodes.rationale: Every part of the JDBC URL is env-overridable with local defaults (localhost:5432/booking_system, user bookingadmin); the password default is empty so a real value must come from the environment. Password value redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto: validate
nodes.rationale: Hibernate is forbidden from mutating the schema; it only checks that entities match what the migrations produced.

nodes.label: spring.flyway.locations: classpath:db/migration + baseline-on-migrate: true
nodes.rationale: Flyway is the sole owner of schema evolution; baseline-on-migrate lets migrations run against a database that already has objects but no Flyway history table.

nodes.label: spring.jpa.show-sql: false
nodes.rationale: SQL logging off by default to keep production logs readable.

nodes.label: spring.mvc.throw-exception-if-no-handler-found: true
nodes.rationale: Makes an unmatched route raise an exception the global handler can turn into a clean JSON 404 instead of Spring's default whitelabel/static fallthrough.

nodes.label: spring.web.resources.add-mappings: false
nodes.rationale: Disables the static-resource handler so unknown paths do not get swallowed by the resource resolver; pairs with throw-exception-if-no-handler-found to make 404s real.

nodes.label: spring.mail host/port (EMAIL_HOST default smtp.gmail.com, EMAIL_PORT default 465)
nodes.rationale: Gmail SMTP on 465 chosen as the confirmation-email transport; both host and port stay env-overridable.

nodes.label: spring.mail username/password (EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASS)
nodes.rationale: Gmail account + app password supplied only via environment; defaults are empty strings. Values redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: [mail.smtp.auth]: true (bracket-quoted YAML key)
nodes.rationale: JavaMail property names contain dots, so they must be written as bracket-quoted single keys rather than nested YAML maps or Spring will not pass them through.

nodes.label: [mail.smtp.ssl.enable]: true (implicit SSL, not STARTTLS)
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS on 587 - this property, not starttls.enable, is what makes JavaMail use SSL for the initial connection.

nodes.label: SMTP timeouts: connectiontimeout / timeout / writetimeout = 10000 ms
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: JavaMail has no default timeout, so a slow/hanging Gmail connection would block the booking thread forever; EmailService's try-catch cannot fire until the socket actually throws.

nodes.label: booking.max-horizon-months: 6 (seed default)
nodes.rationale: Seed value only - the admin's live booking horizon is persisted in the single-row AppSettings table and overrides this at runtime (FR-14/FR-15).

nodes.label: booking.provider-advance-multiplier: 1.5 (not admin-facing)
nodes.rationale: Providers may pre-load availability further ahead than consumers can book; advance limit = ceil(max-horizon-months * multiplier). Deliberately yaml-only so admins cannot change it from the UI.

nodes.label: AppSettings single-row table (runtime override of booking policy)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated single-row table (not a generic key/value store) holds the admin's live horizon so it survives restarts and applies immediately.

nodes.label: EmailService (named in the SMTP timeout comment)
nodes.rationale: Referenced by the config comment as the component whose try-catch depends on the socket timeouts to ever fire.

nodes.label: google.client-id / google.client-secret (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)
nodes.rationale: Bound early (M6, FR-6/FR-13) even before the provider-onboarding controller existed; comment notes it is safe to bind now. Values redacted/env-only, defaults empty.

nodes.label: google.redirect-uri (GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, default http://localhost:8080/api/google/oauth2/callback)
nodes.rationale: Local default points at the dev backend so the OAuth loop works without env setup; production value comes from the Render Blueprint.

nodes.label: google.scope: calendar.events + userinfo.email
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: calendar.events creates/manages the Meet-enabled event; userinfo.email exists purely so the UI can show which Google account is connected.

nodes.label: google.token-encryption-key (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Per-provider Google refresh tokens are stored encrypted at rest, so a separate key is needed beyond the JWT secret. Value redacted/env-only.

nodes.label: app.jwt.secret (JWT_SECRET)
nodes.rationale: Signing key for the M2 JWT bearer auth; env-only with an empty default. Value redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: app.jwt.expiration-ms: 86400000 (24h)
nodes.rationale: 24-hour session length - long enough that a demo run never gets logged out mid-flow.

nodes.label: app.cors.allowed-origins (APP_CORS_ORIGINS, default http://localhost:3000)
nodes.rationale: Split frontend/backend deployment means CORS must be explicitly allowed; the default matches the Next.js dev server so local dev needs no env var.

nodes.label: FR-14 / FR-15 (admin-configurable booking horizon)
nodes.rationale: Requirement IDs cited directly in the config comment, tying the booking keys back to the SRS.

nodes.label: FR-6 / FR-13 (Google Calendar / Meet link generation, milestone M6)
nodes.rationale: Requirement IDs cited in the google block comment.

nodes.label: Flyway owns the schema; Hibernate only validates
nodes.rationale: Migrations are the single source of truth for DDL; ddl-auto: validate turns any entity/schema drift into a startup failure rather than a silent auto-alter.

nodes.label: Two-window booking policy (consumer horizon vs provider advance limit)
nodes.rationale: Consumers book within [today, today+horizon] while providers may pre-load availability up to ceil(horizon*multiplier) ahead, so the rolling window always has slots ready to become bookable.

nodes.label: JSON-only error surface (no static fallthrough, no whitelabel page)
nodes.rationale: A pure API backend consumed by a separate Next.js frontend should never answer with HTML; disabling resource mappings and forcing no-handler exceptions guarantees every miss is a JSON error.

nodes.label: RTL / Arabic support baked into the design tokens
nodes.rationale: Typography tokens ship an RTL font swap (IBM Plex Sans Arabic alongside Inter) so direction changes do not require per-component overrides.

nodes.label: Design-System-first outcome (components over per-screen mockups)
nodes.rationale: Only 4 reference screens exist rather than one per page; remaining pages are composed from the shared components, which the README calls the intended outcome.

nodes.label: Backend HELP.md (Spring Boot 4.1.0 reference links)
nodes.rationale: Initializr-generated pointer file; documents the Maven parent-override gotcha (empty <license>/<developers> overrides must be removed if the parent POM is swapped) and links the exact 4.1.0 docs for Web, Security, Data JPA, Validation and Java Mail Sender.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md - 'This is NOT the Next.js you know'
nodes.rationale: The installed Next.js has breaking changes versus model training data, so the rule mandates reading node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing any page code and heeding deprecation notices.

nodes.label: Frontend CLAUDE.md (single @AGENTS.md import)
nodes.rationale: Kept to a one-line import so the Next.js rules live in exactly one place and cannot drift between the two files.

nodes.label: Frontend README (create-next-app default, dev server on :3000)
nodes.rationale: Untouched create-next-app boilerplate; its localhost:3000 dev server is the origin the backend CORS default allows.

nodes.label: BookIt Design System (pulled from Claude Design via DesignSync)
nodes.rationale: Synced component library rather than hand-written CSS, so design tokens stay the single source of truth shared with the Claude Design project.

nodes.label: tokens/colors.css (teal primary + availability-pressure scale + light/dark)
nodes.rationale: The availability-pressure scale is a first-class token family so calendar pressure colors are derived from the palette instead of disrupting it.

nodes.label: tokens/typography.css (Inter + IBM Plex Sans Arabic, RTL font swap)
ds/styles.css (imports all tokens + component CSS)
nodes.rationale: One aggregate stylesheet so the app has a single global import point.

nodes.label: components/components.css (class-based bk-* styling)
nodes.rationale: Components are styled by bk-* classes rather than inline styles, keeping the synced CSS replaceable on the next DesignSync pull.

nodes.label: @/components/ds barrel export (ES-module React components)
nodes.rationale: A single barrel import is the supported entry point, in contrast to the reference screens which rely on Claude Design sandbox globals.

nodes.label: DS components are untyped .jsx (allowJs on)
nodes.rationale: Synced components arrive as plain JSX; allowJs keeps them usable from the TypeScript app, with prop types added only when composing pages.

nodes.label: screens-reference/ - visual reference only, NOT importable
nodes.rationale: They use Claude Design sandbox globals (window.BookItDesignSystem_* / window.BookItKit) instead of ES imports, so building real pages means swapping globals for @/components/ds imports and mock data for API data.

nodes.label: DS component: CalendarDayCell
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built cell for the booking calendar; the availability-pressure color scale exists in the tokens specifically to drive it.
